strings.name: Hiroshi Ishiguro
strings.role: Robotics researcher and University of Osaka professor
strings.summary: Hiroshi Ishiguro uses androids to study communication, presence and human cognition, including his likeness Geminoid and the ERICA conversational platform. At Osaka and ATR he researches robots, while AVITA explores remote avatars and services. He produced Expo 2025's Future of Life pavilion and extended it to Tokyo in 2026, bringing technology into public debate about life and society.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Studies androids and human–robot interaction, stimulating public debate about robots' social roles, presence and communication.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Computer science bachelor's, Yamanashi; engineering doctorate, Osaka
strings.highlights.h1.title: Studying human communication with robots
strings.highlights.h1.text: Geminoid teleoperated robots and the multi-institution ERICA project explore the social effects of appearance, motion and dialogue.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Research as public experience
strings.highlights.h2.text: He connects robots, avatars and future society through commercial services and Expo exhibitions.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Tokyo exhibition and dialogue
strings.timeline.t1.text: During Future of Life+, he discussed robots and ideas of life with Yoichi Ochiai.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Producing the Expo pavilion
strings.timeline.t2.text: He produced Future of Life at Expo 2025 Osaka, exploring coexistence of people and technology.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Establishing AVITA
strings.timeline.t3.text: He created a company applying avatar, robot and remote-interaction research to service settings.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Team unveils ERICA
strings.timeline.t4.text: Osaka, Kyoto and ATR developed an android research platform for conversation in limited settings.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Systems Innovation professorship
strings.timeline.t5.text: He became professor in Osaka's Graduate School of Engineering Science, Systems Innovation department.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Geminoid HI-1 introduced
strings.timeline.t6.text: He developed a remotely operated robot modeled on himself to study presence and communication.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Osaka doctorate
strings.timeline.t7.text: He completed the Engineering Science doctoral program and earned an engineering doctorate.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Yamanashi graduation
strings.timeline.t8.text: He completed computer science in its engineering faculty before graduate study.
